title: Garden and Tide
premise: Jude Dravenmoor has spent ten years writing anonymous letters to a stranger she met once on a storm-swept pier, never signing her name, certain that a lighthouse keeper's granddaughter with a stalled novel and a dying village had nothing to offer someone like them. When the letters' recipient, Wren Calloway, buys the crumbling cottage next door and begins dismantling Jude's careful invisibility, Jude must decide whether to confess or let Wren leave forever when their publishing career calls them back to London. As the lighthouse is scheduled for decommission and the village rallies to save it, Jude finally signs her name—and discovers Wren has known all along, having moved next door for her. In the end, Jude chooses neither career nor person but a life rebuilt around both: she finishes her novel, the lighthouse becomes a writers' retreat, and she and Wren keep writing letters—now delivered by hand.
about_author: I. M. Vane is the pen name of a former coastal archivist who spent seven years cataloguing lighthouse logs before turning to fiction. They write from a converted signal station on the northern coast, where they claim every manuscript is salt-tested before submission.

chapters.title: The Last Keeper's Granddaughter
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude tends the automated lighthouse her grandfather once kept, writing her unsent novel and her tenth anniversary letter to an unnamed stranger. Establishes her ritual of anonymity and her belief that timing has passed her by. Emotional beat: wistful self-protection.

chapters.title: A Moving Van in Low Season
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. A removal van arrives at the derelict Harrow cottage next door; Jude watches from the lantern room, recognizing the stranger from the pier a decade ago—Wren Calloway, now recognizable from book jacket photos. She hides before they can see her. Emotional beat: panic disguised as curiosity.

chapters.title: Borrowed Sugar, Borrowed Time
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren knocks on Jude's door with a housewarming excuse, having recognized the cottage address from years of return postmarks. Jude plays hostess while concealing everything. Wren notices the typewriter ribbon and the tide charts. Emotional beat: two people performing normalcy.

chapters.title: What the Letters Never Said
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Alone, Wren rereads the full decade of letters, revealing how much of their life was shaped by an anonymous correspondent's encouragement through grief and career failure. Flashbacks show the pier meeting. Emotional beat: longing sharpened into resolve.

chapters.title: The Village That Forgot Its Own Name
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The pub hosts a meeting about the lighthouse's decommission; Jude speaks publicly for the first time in years, surprising herself. Wren volunteers to help the preservation campaign, binding themselves to the village—and to Jude's orbit. Emotional beat: reluctant belonging.

chapters.title: Salt and Ink
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Working side by side on the campaign, Jude and Wren fall into easy rhythm; Jude drafts a letter she cannot send, now that its recipient sleeps forty feet away. Her agent calls: a publisher wants her unfinished novel—if she can finish it in three months. Emotional beat: hope arriving as pressure.

chapters.title: Storm Warning
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. A gale traps Jude and Wren in the lantern room overnight repairing the beacon. Confessions edge closer; Wren nearly reveals why they really came, then retreats. Jude tells a half-truth about knowing 'someone who used to write letters.' Emotional beat: intimacy at the edge of exposure.

chapters.title: The Manuscript in the Drawer
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude writes furiously, and the novel turns out to be about the pier meeting—thinly veiled. Wren finds pages drying on the line and reads three paragraphs before returning them, shaken, saying nothing. Emotional beat: dread of being seen without consent.

chapters.title: An Old Friend of the Family
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren's editor arrives unannounced, pushing Wren to return to London for a career-defining project. Wren stalls, claiming roots here. Jude overhears part of the argument and misreads it as confirmation that Wren will leave. Emotional beat: jealousy wearing the mask of indifference.

chapters.title: Petitions and Postmarks
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The preservation campaign gains traction via a viral letter—written by Wren, quoting Jude's words from the anonymous correspondence. Jude recognizes her own sentences and realizes Wren has treasured them all along. Emotional beat: terror and tenderness entangled.

chapters.title: Low Tide, High Stakes
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. At low tide on the old pier, Jude almost tells Wren everything; instead she asks what would make them stay. Wren answers honestly: 'Someone who stopped hiding.' Jude flees. Emotional beat: the cost of a withheld truth made physical.

chapters.title: The Editor's Offer
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren accepts the London project with a departure date—six weeks out—and begins quietly packing hope away. Meanwhile they submit Jude's salvaged manuscript pages to their editor under a pseudonym, a betrayal meant as a gift. Emotional beat: love making reckless choices.

chapters.title: Deadline Weather
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude learns her pseudonymous pages are with a publisher—her words, taken without permission. Confrontation on the cliff path: accusations, Wren's counter-accusation that Jude has been lying for a decade. Both retreat wounded. Emotional beat: the midpoint rupture.

chapters.title: Silence Between Signals
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Two weeks of cold civility; campaign work continues through gritted teeth. Jude writes chapter after chapter of the novel's ending, unable to finish it because she no longer knows if it deserves one. Wren drafts a resignation letter and deletes it nightly. Emotional beat: grief for something never declared.

chapters.title: Grandmother's Trunk
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Clearing her late grandmother's things, Jude finds the original letters' first draft—signed—and a note from her grandmother: 'Invisibility is just fear with better posture.' Jude understands the inheritance she actually received. Emotional beat: generational absolution.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The council hearing on the lighthouse; Jude gives the closing testimony, publicly reading from her own anonymous letters as evidence of what the light means. Wren realizes, mid-room, that the correspondent is standing in front of them. Emotional beat: public revelation, private devastation.

chapters.title: You Knew My Words Before You Knew Me
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Aftermath confrontation at the cottage: Wren admits they knew for months—that the move was always for Jude. Fury and relief collide; Jude slams the door anyway, needing to choose freely rather than be chosen by ambush. Emotional beat: climax of truth without resolution.

chapters.title: The Night the Light Went Out
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Decommission day. The village gathers as the beam goes dark; Jude climbs alone and lights the old backup lamp by hand, one last keeper's act. She finishes the final page of her novel on the lantern room floor. Emotional beat: mourning transmuted into authorship.

chapters.title: Platform Nine, Wrong Direction
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren boards the train to London, then gets off at the first stop and turns back, resigning by phone from a payphone in the rain. Not for Jude—for the version of themselves that existed in these letters. Emotional beat: choosing oneself first, so love can follow.

chapters.title: Signed at Last
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude slips the finished novel and a signed letter—the eleventh—under Wren's door, then waits on the pier where it began. Wren comes at dusk carrying a reply written long ago and never sent. First kiss, no more masks. Emotional beat: release.

chapters.title: Keepers of Something Brighter
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Months later: the lighthouse reopens as a writers' retreat; the village, the campaign, and the two of them have built something none planned. Jude's novel is accepted; Wren takes only freelance work. Emotional beat: found family solidifying into home.

chapters.title: Delivered by Hand
chapters.summary: Jude's POV, coda. On the first anniversary of the dark, Jude and Wren exchange letters across the garden wall—then burn them unread, keeping only this year's, written together. Final image: two names signed on one page, the light room glowing again for the festival. Emotional beat: quiet, earned joy.
